headline: Italy's Garante fined Meta 805 million euros over Facebook's default access to Android photo galleries, while Cursor traced its poisoned Claude Code extension to a single access key Fireworks AI left exposed.

emerging_trends.text: Cursor traced the trojanized Claude Code extension in its marketplace to one access key that Fireworks AI left exposed, which shows how a single credential sitting at an AI infrastructure provider reaches every developer downstream.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Stolen Fireworks Key Opened Cursor's Marketplace

emerging_trends.text: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet hands agents a stand-in card number to spend with, the same week Token Security demonstrated an invoice-processing agent that a malicious email steers into rewriting vendor bank details, so agents now carry money authority ahead of the controls that would bound it.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Agents Get Spending Power Before Controls Catch Up

emerging_trends.text: Italy's Garante attached 805 million euros to a single default-on setting inside Facebook for Android, which puts a European price on the consent defaults mobile apps have carried for years.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Italy Fines Meta Over Facebook Gallery Access

topics.title: Italy Fines Meta Over Facebook Gallery Access
topics.latest_developments: The Garante, Italy's data protection authority, fined Meta 805 million euros, about $887 million, on November 14, 2026, finding that Facebook for Android read Italian users' photos, videos, and related metadata without explicit consent, and gave the company 60 days.
topics.summary: Facebook for Android suggests photos and videos out of a user's phone gallery as post material, and the feature arrives switched on. The Garante cited a European directive that treats a smartphone as part of a person's private sphere and demands free and informed consent before an app reaches into it.

sources.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
Meta Fined $887 Million in Italy Over Android Gallery Photos and Videos on Facebook

topics.title: Stolen Fireworks Key Opened Cursor's Marketplace
topics.latest_developments: Cursor said in a Friday, November 13, 2026 update that the attacker obtained an access key Cursor itself had issued to Fireworks AI, that Fireworks exposed the key, and that the attacker used it to copy data from a read-only source.
topics.summary: Attackers distributed a malicious version of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension through Cursor's extension marketplace, working from credentials stolen in the breach at Fireworks AI, the AI infrastructure provider. Developers who installed the extension should rotate every credential the editor could reach.

sources.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension

topics.title: Pentagon Renames the CDAO
topics.latest_developments: The Department of Defense renamed its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office the Super Intelligence Office, following President Trump's order that executive branch communications replace the phrase artificial intelligence with super intelligence.
topics.summary: The CDAO runs the Pentagon's data, analytics, and AI programs, including the model evaluation and deployment work that military cyber operations draw on. The rename reaches contractors and program documents that cite the office by name.

sources.title: Pentagon Renames CDAO ‘Super Intelligence Office’

topics.title: Agents Get Spending Power Before Controls Catch Up
topics.latest_developments: OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT Wallet, built with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, which pays merchants through a stand-in card number so a user's real card details reach neither the agent nor the merchant, and Token Security published five enterprise gaps it found while testing an invoice-processing agent that a malicious email could push into changing a vendor's bank details with no alert firing.
topics.summary: Agents now hold payment authority and finance workflows inside companies, and the identity and approval controls around them lag the capability. Token Security's guidance and OpenAI's stand-in card both aim at the same problem: an agent that acts with a person's authority and no bounded credential.

sources.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents pay without seeing your card number
How one AI agent exposed five critical enterprise security gaps
Is AI Making Us Worse at Cybersecurity?

topics.title: Apple Details Secure Exclaves for Camera and Mic
topics.latest_developments: Apple published the architecture of Secure Exclaves, which isolates camera and microphone data from the main operating system on HomeView and the newest iPhones, so a compromise of iOS alone leaves ambient sensor data out of an attacker's reach.
topics.summary: Secure Exclaves fence off the hardware that watches and listens, keeping that data inside a separate execution environment rather than the general-purpose operating system. The design matters most for always-on home devices, where a single operating system flaw would otherwise open a live camera and microphone.

sources.title: Apple Reveals How Secure Exclaves Shield Camera and Microphone Data

topics.title: A 22-Year-Old PostgreSQL Bug Runs Code
topics.latest_developments: The worst flaw in this week's PostgreSQL release now carries a number and an age: CVE-2026-6460, a type confusion bug rated 8.8 that has sat in the code for 22 years and lets any database user who can create objects run commands on the server with the rights of the operating system account.
topics.summary: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group closed 52 vulnerabilities on November 12, 2026 across versions 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25. Patching alone leaves a gap: administrators must also rebuild every C-language extension installed on the server.

sources.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE

business_politics.title: The AI Trade Unravels
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Sunday, November 15, that shares in the data center construction companies at the center of the artificial-intelligence build-out have lost $4.2 trillion in value, with Nvidia's quarterly results this week and Anthropic's coming initial public offering the next two tests of the trade.
business_politics.summary: Money has rotated out of the "picks and shovels" suppliers that build, wire, and power data centers and into defensive sectors, the Financial Times found. Anthropic plans to sell shares to the public this month, and individual investors told the Wall Street Journal they feel compelled to buy a company whose technology they distrust, one describing the offering as "almost like the last chopper out of Saigon."

business_politics.title: Congress Moves on Chip Exports
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Sunday, November 15, that Congress now moves to pass tighter export controls on artificial-intelligence chips, with lawmakers saying Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese intelligence agent "increases momentum" for a crackdown on American hardware reaching China.
business_politics.summary: Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive on November 12, and finance chief Colette Kress runs the company while the board searches for a successor. The Wall Street Journal reported Sunday that the enormous data centers Nvidia helped stand up in Southeast Asia fed Chinese companies crucial computing power and gave cover to alleged chip smuggling, a backdoor that kept Beijing in the artificial-intelligence race.

business_politics.title: Iran Hits Bahrain a Second Time This Week
business_politics.latest_developments: Bahrain said Sunday, November 15, that it destroyed a second barrage of Iranian drones in a week, and the Wall Street Journal reported that American estimates now put Tehran's rebuilt missile stockpile at as many as 2,500, a figure that contradicts President Trump's public assertions and feeds the administration's debate over resuming strikes.
business_politics.summary: Iran has struck the island kingdom, which hosts the United States Navy's Fifth Fleet, repeatedly since the war with Washington began, and this week's attacks break months of relative calm in the Gulf. The United States military shot down two Iranian attack drones Friday, November 13, after Iran claimed a strike on an American radar installation there.

sources.title: Iran attacks Bahrain in escalation of Gulf hostilities
Iran Targets Bahrain Again After Resuming Attacks on U.S. Ally

business_politics.title: One Router in Southern Arkansas
business_politics.latest_developments: Airlines scrapped hundreds more departures Sunday, November 15, a third straight day of disruption, and the Wall Street Journal traced the whole collapse to a single router in southern Arkansas that a data overload knocked out on an antiquated Federal Aviation Administration network.
business_politics.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration halted every departing flight in the country Friday afternoon, November 13, stalling hundreds of thousands of travelers, and investigators have centered on the contractor L3Harris and a job replacing copper wire. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed Congress and demanded $50 billion to rebuild air traffic control, and the Financial Times reported that decades of bipartisan neglect left the pilot-controller communications system unfit for its job.

sources.title: Ground Stop Ripples Into Third Day of Scrapped Flights
The Single Router in Southern Arkansas That Ground Air Travel to a Halt

business.title: Faucher Likes the Holiday Sales Outlook
business.latest_developments: Gus Faucher used his Economist's View column in the Post-Gazette on Sunday, November 15, to argue that the outlook for holiday sales looks good despite the gloom around consumers.
business.summary: Faucher, the chief economist at Pittsburgh-based PNC Financial Services Group, writes the Post-Gazette's Economist's View column, and his read on household spending sets expectations for Western Pennsylvania retailers heading into Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26.

sources.title: Economist’s View: Believe it or not, outlook looks good for holiday sales

business.title: The $1.7 Billion Terminal at One Year
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette asked Sunday, November 15, whether Pittsburgh International Airport's $1.7 billion terminal, now one year old, earned its price.
business.summary: The Allegheny County Airport Authority opened the building in November 2025, moving ticketing, security screening, and baggage claim next to the gates in Findlay Township. Its first anniversary weekend brought dozens of cancellations and delays as the airport dug out from the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop.

sources.title: One year in: Was the new Pittsburgh International Airport terminal worth building?

around_town.title: Pittsburgh International Digs Out
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh International Airport ran dozens of cancellations and delays through Saturday, November 14, as crews and airlines rebuilt schedules wrecked by Friday's nationwide ground stop, and the Federal Aviation Administration expects national travel to recover before the weekend ends.
around_town.summary: KDKA's Ricky Sayer reported from the terminal in Findlay Township on a day travelers spent rebooking and waiting. The Federal Aviation Administration grounded every departing United States flight Friday afternoon, November 13, after communications failed at regional air traffic control centers.

sources.title: Pittsburgh International Airport sees dozens of cancellations, delays as airport rebounds from FAA ground stop

around_town.latest_developments: Light scattered snow showers and morning rain moved across the Pittsburgh area Sunday, November 15, in what WTAE calls the final day of the lake-effect setup, with a chilly, cloudy afternoon behind it.
around_town.summary: KDKA meteorologist Mary Ours opened Sunday with chilly temperatures and scattered snow showers, and WPXI reported that a few flakes mix in around the city while the steadier snow falls over the Laurel Highlands and the Allegheny Mountains.

around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published an account Sunday, November 15, of how sports betting has reshaped the finances and habits of young men across Western Pennsylvania.
around_town.summary: The piece lands as wagering runs through every Steelers broadcast, including Sunday night's game at Cincinnati, and follows PublicSource's finding last week that Pennsylvania's self-exclusion rolls now reach far beyond the counties that host casinos.

events.title: Richard Lloyd Dies at 75
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, November 13, that Richard Lloyd, the Pittsburgh native who played guitar for the New York band Television, has died at 75.
events.summary: Lloyd grew up in Pittsburgh and built his name downtown at CBGB in Manhattan, where Television's twin-guitar sound, captured on the 1977 album "Marquee Moon," shaped American rock for the next half century.

sources.title: Richard Lloyd, Pittsburgh native and guitarist for acclaimed NYC rockers Television, dies at 75

events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, November 13, that Pittsburgh plays a starring role in the new film "How to Rob a Bank."
events.summary: The production joins a long run of movies that use Pittsburgh's bridges, hillsides, and downtown blocks as more than a backdrop, and the Post-Gazette walks through the locations city audiences will recognize.

around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette examined Sunday, November 15, the central collision of the Steelers' trip to Cincinnati: the Bengals thrive on explosive passing plays, and the Steelers defense excels at stopping them.

around_teams.latest_developments: Gerry Dulac published his Week 10 NFL predictions in the Post-Gazette on Sunday morning, November 15, picking the full slate with Pittsburgh at Cincinnati as the Sunday night game.

team_usa.title: Pochettino's Farewell Begins
team_usa.latest_developments: Mauricio Pochettino said after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti, November 14, that the United States men's national team has an "amazing future," and ESPN reported Sunday that his players intend to carry his standards forward in the penultimate match of his tenure.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino leaves for Manchester United on November 17, and Steve Cherundolo takes the December camp on an interim basis; the return leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti closes out the Argentine's run. Christian Pulisic scored twice in the first leg and drew a 9 out of 10 in ESPN's player ratings, and teenage forward Julian Hall tied himself to the United States over Poland by starting.

team_usa.title: Malinin Wins a Fourth Skate America
team_usa.latest_developments: Ilia Malinin won Skate America for the fourth time Saturday night, November 14, opening what ESPN calls a four-year run toward the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps.
team_usa.summary: Malinin, 21, scored 96.74 points in Friday's short program to lead his first Grand Prix outing of the season, and he built that program as a tribute to the members of the skating community killed in January 2025 when their American Airlines flight collided with a military helicopter near Washington.

team_usa.title: Harrison's Case for the UFC
team_usa.latest_developments: Bryan Armen Graham argued in the Guardian on Sunday, November 15, that Kayla Harrison's career makes the UFC hard to dismiss even as the company squeezes fighters, bullies journalists, and courts President Trump.
team_usa.summary: Harrison won Olympic judo gold for the United States in 2012 and 2016, sports that paid their champions almost nothing, and she now headlines for a promotion that gave athletes from neglected Olympic disciplines a route to real money and fame. Trump publicly floated UFC Chief Executive Dana White for a role in his administration last week.
